reason: Attacked and held. I downloaded Project Gutenberg 2446, whose header names the translator R. Farquharson Sharp, and read the end of ACT V (the file's act headings run ACT I to ACT V; the play ends at the last of them). The text reads, with the em dash: Dr. Stockmann (Gathers them round him, and says confidentially:) It is this, let me tell you-that the strongest man in the world is he who stands most alone. That is the candidate word for word, including he who and not the man who, which is the drift I went looking for. It is Dr Stockmann's last speech, and exactly two speeches follow: Mrs. Stockmann (smiling and shaking her head) Oh, Thomas, Thomas! and Petra (encouragingly, as she grasps her father's hands) Father! So the verifier's correction is right on both counts, and the curtain line is Petra's. The edition named in the evidence also checks out: Everyman's Library 552, Ghosts, The Warriors at Helgeland, An Enemy of the People, translated with an introduction by R. Farquharson Sharp, J. M. Dent, first published 1911. shipped.js: not shipped, no near match, Ibsen banned=false, one of three (month 3). Source line is 111 characters, leads with Ibsen, no em dash, no straight quote, speaker in parentheses after the locator, translator and year at the end; Drama is the form. One honest caveat that does not reach refutation: the note does not say what this points back to, namely the great discovery Stockmann announces two speeches earlier, nor that Ibsen gives it to a man in the middle of a self-congratulating scene. A sentence to that effect would make the note fuller, but nothing in the citation is wrong.
